summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic ER+ breast cancer involving the liver and bones was admitted with severe chest pain worsened by breathing and movement. A CT angiogram revealed a sternal fracture with a small retrosternal hematoma, likely due to malignancy, and a small right pleural effusion. She was experiencing acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, managed with supplemental oxygen initially, and was weaned to room air. Pain was poorly controlled on home morphine, so her dose was increased to 30 mg every 8 hours with Dilaudid for breakthrough pain. This led to opioid-induced ileus, which was managed with magnesium citrate and a reduction in breakthrough opioid. A new T11 vertebral compression fracture was identified on follow-up imaging. Her pain regimen was optimized, and she was discharged home with an adjusted opioid schedule, a bowel regimen, and plans to resume Taxol chemotherapy the following week.
problems: Pathological fracture in neoplastic disease, other specified site, initial encounter for fracture
Secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct
Malignant neoplasm of unspecified site of right female breast
